name: Family Reunification (Spouse/Registered Partner)

requirements.blocker_text: Available to the spouse or registered partner of a person holding a Finnish residence permit or Finnish citizenship. Marriage certificate required (legalised if from outside the Nordics/EU); gender-neutral, applies equally to registered partnerships.

For applications from 16 June 2025 onward, both spouses must be at least 21 years old when the residence permit becomes valid; applications may be submitted up to 9 months before turning 21, but validity cannot start before both reach 21.

Sponsor's net monthly income must meet the regional threshold: EUR 1,210 (Helsinki metro area), EUR 1,090 (other large municipalities), or EUR 1,030 (other municipalities) for a single adult, plus per-dependent add-ons. Income cannot be based on social assistance, labour market subsidy, or general unemployment benefit; salary, business income, pensions, assets, rental income, and dividends count.

evidence_required.document: Marriage or registered-partnership certificate (legalised if applicable)
Sponsor's residence permit or citizenship proof
Proof of sponsor's income meeting the regional threshold

outcome.duration_length: typically matches the sponsor's permit type/duration

sources.title: Maahanmuuttovirasto -- Spouse in Finland with a Residence Permit: income requirement, marriage certificate, 21-year minimum age (from 16 June 2025), fees

Maahanmuuttovirasto -- Income Requirement for Family Members: regional net-income thresholds effective 1 November 2024 (Helsinki metro / other large municipalities / other municipalities), per-dependent add-ons

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Finland). income threshold modeled at the lowest regional figure (EUR 1,030, other municipalities) as the baseline hard requirement, with the higher Helsinki-area and large-municipality figures disclosed in blocker_text rather than as separate requirement groups, since the underlying condition (meeting your specific region's threshold) is the same rule applied regionally, not a structurally different route. A 21-year minimum age for both spouses (effective for applications from 16 June 2025) is an unusually high bar compared to most countries in this dataset -- flagged explicitly, as it functions as an anti-forced-marriage/anti-fraud measure per the broader EU policy context, though this framing was not independently confirmed as Migri's own stated rationale.
